title: State renaming preserves a step
statement: Let $S$ and $H$ be state sets, let $\Gamma$ be a symbol alphabet, and let $M_S$ and $M_H$ be nondeterministic machines with $k$ work tapes and state sets $S$ and $H$, respectively. Let $e:S\hookrightarrow H$ be an embedding and let $G\subseteq S$. Suppose that for each choice bit, every state $q\in G$, and every input and work-tape observation, the transition of $M_H$ at $e(q)$ is the state-renamed transition of $M_S$ at $q$. If $c$ is a configuration of $M_S$ on input $x$ and every state present in $c$ belongs to $G$, then stepping the renamed configuration $e(c)$ in $M_H$ gives the state-renamed result of stepping $c$ in $M_S$, for every choice bit.
hypotheses_covered: Two nondeterministic machines with $k$ work tapes
